attorneys.name: Malcolm M. Crosland Jr.
attorneys.practice_type: Worker's Compensation Lawyers in North Charleston, SC
attorneys.bio:
Malcolm Crosland has been in practice for 34 years, and that’s no surprise. He comes from a family of lawyers — his father and grandfather were lawyers, so carrying on the family tradition was a natural path for him to take. You could almost call it predestined. He handles personal injury cases, including auto and truck accidents, nursing home abuse, medical malpractice, brain injuries, slip-and-fall cases, drug recalls, and wrongful death suits.

Known for his honesty, compassion, integrity, and zealous pursuit of justice, Malcolm appreciates his clients and considers them family. When it comes to handling personal injury cases, he understands how an accident or the death of a loved one can affect an entire family. Nowadays, he applies his career-long experience and insights to working on behalf of first responders and healthcare providers whose livelihoods, medical status, and finances have been affected by the COVID-19 pandemic. He represents his clients in state and federal courts, the South Carolina Worker's Compensation Commission, and the U.S. Department of Labor, and is responsible for numerous published appellate decisions in both state and federal courts.

Malcolm attended the University of South Carolina for his undergraduate work and its School of Law for his legal training. “I was drawn to the Steinberg Law Firm’s reputation for representing injured workers and their families,” he said of his decision to join the firm immediately after graduating from law school in 1986.

Recognized year after year by Best Lawyers in America and Super Lawyers, Malcolm also holds an A/V (the highest level) rating with Martindale-Hubbell for his professional and ethical standards. He has received recognition in Best Lawyers in South Carolina every year since 2009.

Malcolm is passionate about giving back to the community and has served on both charitable boards and law-related committees. He has served on the board of directors of the Brain Injury Association of South Carolina and of Lowcountry AIDS Services; is the former president of the Barrier Islands Free Medical Clinic; and currently is president of Workers Injury Law and Advocacy, a national organization whose mission is to protect the rights of working people.

Malcolm grew up the village of Mount Pleasant, just a few blocks from Charleston’s harbor. When he isn’t working on behalf of his law clients or community, he enjoys traveling, spending time with his family, reading, fishing the waters around Charleston, surfing, cooking, or playing golf.

attorneys.name: Nathan M. Crystal
attorneys.practice_type: Professional Responsibility Lawyers in Charleston, SC
attorneys.bio:
Nathan Crystal is a Distinguished Visiting Professor of Law at the Charleston Law School. He taught for 32 years at the University of South Carolina School of Law until he retired in 2008. On his retirement from South Carolina he was named the Distinguished Class of 1969 Professor of Professional Responsibility and Contract Law Emeritus. He holds degrees from the University of Pennsylvania (Wharton School), Emory Law School (where he was editor-in-chief of the law review), and Harvard Law School. Professor Crystal concentrates in the areas of professional responsibility and contract law.

He is the author or coauthor of four books, three on legal ethics and one on contract law:

PROFESSIONAL RESPONSIBILITY – PROBLEMS OF PRACTICE AND THE PROFESSION (Aspen Law & Business 4th ed. 2008)

AN INTRODUCTION TO PROFESSIONAL RESPONSIBILITY (Aspen Law & Business 1998)

ANNOTATED SOUTH CAROLINA RULES OF PROFESSIONAL CONDUCT (S.C. Bar 2009 ed.) (with Robert M. Wilcox) (forthcoming in June)

PROBLEMS IN CONTRACT LAW: CASES AND MATERIALS (with Charles Knapp and Harry G. Prince) (6th ed. 2007)

In addition to his books, Professor Crystal has published numerous articles in scholarly journals, including the Fordham Law Review, Georgetown Journal of Legal Ethics, Illinois Law Review, Kansas Law Review, Kentucky Law Journal, Mercer Law Review, Notre Dame Journal of Law Ethics and Public Policy, NYU Annual Survey of American Law, Saint Mary's Law Journal, Saint Louis Law Journal, South Carolina Law Review, Wake Forest Law Review, and Washington Law Review. He authors a bimonthly column, "Ethics Watch," for the South Carolina Lawyer. Professor Crystal lectures frequently on matters of professional ethics to national, regional, and local organizations, including the American Bar Association and the United States Justice Department. He has been a member of the South Carolina Bar Ethics Advisory Committee for more than 20 years and served as chair of the Committee from 2002-2003. Professor Crystal was associate dean of the USC Law School from 1987-1992 and director of its Center on the Legal Profession from 1991-1999. He has held visiting appointments and lectureships at Arkansas (Little Rock), Florida State, Hastings, Indiana (Indianapolis), Luiss (Rome), Scuola Superiore Santa'Anna (Pisa), Suffolk, Sydney (Parsons Visiting Scholar). In 2011, he co-cofounded, together with Francesca Giannoni-Crystal, Crystal & Giannoni-Crystal LLC.

attorneys.name: William Shipp Daniel III
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Florence, SC
attorneys.bio:
W. Shipp Daniel III is an associate attorney at Parham Law Firm, where he represents clients in criminal defense and personal injury matters. Working from the firm’s Florence and Georgetown offices, Shipp handles cases from initial consultation through trial and settlement, advocating for individuals facing criminal charges as well as those who have been injured due to the negligence of others.

Before joining Parham Law Firm in 2024, Shipp spent more than fifteen years as an Assistant Solicitor in South Carolina’s Fourth Circuit, prosecuting cases throughout Chesterfield, Darlington, Dillon, and Marlboro counties. During that time, he managed Dillon County’s criminal docket and prosecuted serious felony cases from arrest through final disposition. His experience includes extensive courtroom litigation, including numerous jury trials, as well as advising local and state law enforcement agencies on investigations and charging decisions.

In addition to his prosecutorial work, Shipp has taught at legal seminars and conferences on topics related to criminal prosecution, including trial advocacy and juvenile prosecution, sharing practical courtroom strategies and experience with fellow attorneys and prosecutors.

Shipp’s background as a career prosecutor gives him a unique perspective on how criminal cases are investigated, built, and tried. He now uses that experience to defend individuals accused of crimes and to advocate for clients who have been seriously injured in accidents. His familiarity with the strategies used by prosecutors and insurance companies allows him to anticipate challenges and develop effective legal strategies for his clients.

Prior to his work as a prosecutor, Shipp served as a law clerk to the Honorable James E. Lockemy of the South Carolina Circuit Court, where he conducted legal research, reviewed motions, and assisted in drafting judicial orders.

Shipp earned his Juris Doctor from the University of South Carolina School of Law, where he participated in Moot Court. He graduated magna cum laude from Clemson University, earning a Bachelor of Arts. While at Clemson, Shipp worked in the Sports Information Department primarily with the football and women’s basketball teams as the liaison between the teams and the media. He refereed men’s college basketball (Junior College to Division I) from 2010 to 2024.

attorneys.bio:
Dakota Julius Derrick was born and raised in Conway, SC. He attended Furman University on a football scholarship and played quarterback for the Paladins. After Furman, Dakota attended the University of South Carolina School of Law. During his time there, Dakota helped revive the school's mock trial team, competing alongside fellow Derrick Law Firm attorney Taylor Hooven in several national competitions. It was here that Dakota fell in love with the courtroom.

After graduating from the University of South Carolina with honors in 2016, Dakota served two years as a judicial law clerk for Justice John Cannon Few of the South Carolina Supreme Court. Dakota worked with Justice Few on cases involving many areas of the law and assisted Justice Few in writing over two dozen majority and dissenting opinions.

In 2018, Dakota returned home to Conway and joined Derrick Law Firm Injury Lawyers to fulfill his lifelong dream of working alongside his father to represent those in need. Dakota's practice is focused mainly on car wreck cases and trucking cases.

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury -- Plaintiff Lawyers in Conway, SC
attorneys.bio:
Dirk J. Derrick was born in Myrtle Beach, South Carolina in 1960. He grew up in Conway. His first job was at the age of 6 as a farmhand on his grandfather's tobacco farm in rural Horry County. At age 9, he purchased his first vehicle when his grandfather sold him a 1960 pickup truck for the amount Dirk earned that week, $28.00. Dirk credits hot, humid summer days in the tobacco fields as his inspiration to excel in school and get a good education.

He grew up in a house with his parents, Julius and Polly Derrick, and three sisters. His father was a high school teacher and football coach who had been co-captain of the 1957 South Carolina Gamecock football team and drafted by the New York Giants. Coach Derrick was very competitive and his children were raised to compete to win in anything they pursue. Everything was a competition including who could be the most productive in their summertime farming jobs, who could make the best grades in school, and who could win a particular athletic competition. This characteristic probably explains why all four children attended college and participated in college athletics.

Dirk earned a football scholarship to Wofford College where he played for four years. After graduating, he coached college football at East Tennessee State University for one year where he met his wife, Michelle Garrity. They were married in 1985, the same year Dirk began law school at the University of South Carolina. He graduated in 1987 and began practicing in Horry County in 1988. Due to early success in the courtroom, Dirk worked his way into a partnership after just three years. In 1991, he left the partnership and established The Derrick Law Firm.

He and his wife, Michelle, are very involved with their two sons, Dakota and Peyton. Dakota now works as an attorney at The Derrick Law Firm and Peyton plays college football.

Dirk is also very involved with his community. He is a founding member and elder of The Rock, Conway's Community Church which began in 2005 as a ministry for young people, people who have never gone to church, or people who have no interest in attending traditional churches. He is also involved with the Fellowship of Christian Athletes and has been so since he first attended an FCA Camp in Black Mountain, NC as a young man. He has been a member of the Horry County FCA Adult Chapter and has also served on the Coastal Area FCA Board in the past.

Dirk supports the Children's Mentoring Program of Horry County, formerly Big Brothers/Big Sisters of Horry County and was a board member for many years. His father and mother have been the co-directors of the program since 1989.

The Derrick Law Firm also sponsored the Derrick Law Firm Carolinas Kickoff Clash from 2012-2015. This was an interstate football weekend matching South Carolina teams versus North Carolina teams.

The Derrick Law Firm also sponsored the annual Run for the Children 5K Race from 2013-2016. The race runs through historic downtown Conway, and all funds raised were donated to the Children's Mentoring Program of Horry County.

Dirk has focused his practice on personal injury, wrongful death, and worker's compensation cases since he graduated from law school in 1987. He has owned his own practice since 1991 and has expanded from his main office in Conway and added six other offices across South Carolina.

He has also been voted the Best Attorney for the Horry Independent's Readers' Choice Awards for the years 2014-2019. He was also voted Best Attorney for the Myrtle Beach Herald Readers' Choice Awards from 2016-2018. The Derrick Law Firm was voted Best Law Office by the Myrtle Beach Herald Readers' Choice Awards in 2018 and 2019.

attorneys.name: Aaron R. Dias
attorneys.practice_type: Tepezza Hearing Loss Lawsuit Lawyers in Mount Pleasant, SC
attorneys.bio:
Aaron Dias is a member of RPWB’s pharmaceutical litigation team, which fights for the rights of consumers who have been injured or killed by pharmaceutical drugs and medical devices. With a strong scientific background, he also has years of experience in natural resource damage and other toxic tort cases.

He is a 2005 graduate of the University of South Carolina School of Law and a 1994 graduate of the College of Charleston, where he received a B.S. in chemistry and a B.A. in history. Prior to pursuing a law career, he worked for 8 years as a chemist at the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), where he performed environmental chemistry research.

Dias clerked for RPWB during law school and was brought on as an associate in 2005. He was named a member in 2019. In addition to his case work, he manages the firm’s clerkship program.

A native of Charleston, Dias is an avid tennis player. He enjoys travel and escaping the city’s humidity by retreating to the mountains whenever he can. He has two miniature dachshunds, Steffi and Gabby.

attorneys.name: Thomas Drazan
attorneys.firm_name: Derrick Law Firm Injury Lawyers, PC
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Conway, SC
attorneys.bio:
Thomas “Tom” Drazan is passionate about serving clients as a personal injury attorney at Derrick Law Firm Injury Lawyers. Tom, raised near Annapolis, Maryland, is the child of two life-long public educators from whom he learned the value of serving a community.

After arriving in the Lowcountry to attend the College of Charleston in 2005, he knew that he wanted to make South Carolina his home. Tom left the Lowcountry to attend the Southern Methodist University’s Dedman School of Law, promptly returning to Charleston upon graduation.

For the first two years following law school, he worked for a large plaintiff’s firm involved in tobacco, pharmaceutical antitrust, and products liability class action lawsuits. Tom then gained experience at a local defense firm, litigating on behalf of insurance companies for three years. During that time, he litigated in the areas of personal injury, civil rights, fiduciary duty, construction, and a myriad of other cases. Desiring a change in who he served, Tom returned to plaintiffs’ practice to litigate on behalf of individuals and small business owners, not insurance companies.

Tom lives in Charleston and enjoys fly fishing, cooking, and any activity on the water. He is involved in the Neighbors Helping Neighbors Charity that supports the Hollywood community, providing resources for the students of Title 1 schools.

attorneys.name: Brian C. Duffy
attorneys.practice_type: Business Disputes Lawyers in Charleston, SC
attorneys.bio:
Brian C. Duffy is a partner of Nelson Mullins Riley & Scarborough LLP in Charleston. Mr. Duffy's practice focuses primarily on litigation; he also counsels corporate clients regarding other issues their businesses face. Mr. Duffy is a mediator certified by the United States District Court and by the South Carolina Board of Arbitrator and Mediator Certification. In addition, Mr. Duffy serves as an Adjunct Professor of Commercial Law at the Charleston School of Law.

A member of the South Carolina Bar and the District of Columbia Bar, Mr. Duffy is admitted to practice before the Supreme Court of the United States; the U.S. Courts of Appeals for the District of Columbia, Eleventh and Federal Circuits; the U.S. District Courts for the District of South Carolina and the District of Columbia; and the U.S. Court of Federal Claims.

Prior to joining Nelson Mullins in 2004, Mr. Duffy was associated with a leading U.S. law firm in Washington, D.C. During 2000-01, Mr. Duffy served as associate counsel of the Judicial Review Commission on Foreign Assets Control. From 1999 to 2000, he served as a law clerk to U.S. Circuit Judge Karen L. Henderson of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit, and from 1998-99, Mr. Duffy served as a law clerk to U.S. District Judge C. Lynwood Smith, Jr. of the Northern District of Alabama.

During the confirmation hearings of John G. Roberts, Jr. as Chief Justice of the United States, Mr. Duffy submitted written testimony at the invitation of the Chairman of the Senate Committee on the Judiciary. Mr. Duffy also has appeared before the U.S. Supreme Court in a victory on behalf of a national bank.

A member of the American Bar Association, Mr. Duffy is also a member of the Charleston County Bar Association and the South Carolina Defense Attorneys' Association. He is the author of Barring Foul Blows, 50 Vand. L. Rev. 1335 (1997) and the co-author of Admissibility of Expert Testimony: South Carolina's Standard in Relation to and in Light of Daubert, 25:1, The Defense Line, 6 (1997).

In 1998, Mr. Duffy earned a Juris Doctor from the Vanderbilt University School of Law where he was Notes Editor of Vanderbilt Law Review, a John W. Wade Scholar, a member of the Philip C. Jessup International Law Moot Court Competition, and an orator in the Student Scholarship Series. Mr. Duffy earned a Bachelor of Arts in Political Science, with highest distinction, from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill in 1995.

attorneys.name: D. Charles Dukes
attorneys.practice_type: Business Litigation Lawyers in Mount Pleasant, SC
attorneys.bio:
Chuck Dukes is a member of RPWB’s consumer class action group, which represents thousands of individuals in various state and federal courts throughout the country. In addition to his class work, Chuck also represents whistleblowers in qui tam litigation brought under the False Claims Act.

He also litigates serious personal injury cases on behalf of clients who were injured or killed through no fault of their own. For example, Chuck represented the young widow of a man killed by a drunk driver in downtown Charleston, South Carolina. After significant investigation, and extensive litigation, it was determined that two bars had overserved the drunk driver before he caused the fatal collision. The case resolved for $5.4 million just before trial.

A native of North Carolina, Chuck moved to Charleston in 2009 and is magna cum laude graduate of the Charleston School of Law, where he served on the Moot Court Board, Trial Advocacy Board, and was a senior legal writing teaching fellow. He obtained his B.S. in Business Administration from the University of North Carolina at Wilmington. Chuck began his work at RPWB as a summer law clerk, then became an attorney with the firm in 2013.

He and his wife Jenn have two wonderful daughters, Eva, and Elle, and two spirited springer spaniels, Charlie and Lucy. Outside of work, he enjoys running, the great outdoors, building things, gathering with friends, and watching competitive sports.

attorneys.name: Rustin Duncan
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Greer, SC
attorneys.bio:
Rustin Duncan is the managing partner for King Law’s South Carolina offices. He is a lifelong native and resident of Greenville, South Carolina. He works from the firm’s Greer office and covers the Upstate of South Carolina. With fifteen years of experience, Rusty currently practices primarily in the areas of family law, adoptions, juvenile matters, civil litigation, business & employment law, elder law and wills/estates.

Community Involvement

Rusty is a former member of the Tryon Rotary Club and has volunteered legal services for Steps to Hope in the past. He was a member of the Greer Chamber of Commerce and has appeared as a guest speaker at Greer Relief Ministries on legal related topics. He is active in the community. He has been interviewed on News Channel 7 for a law related story and has guest posted on legal blogs.

Rusty previously served on the Board of Directors for the Travelers Rest Historical Society and currently serves as an appointed community member on the School Improvement Committee at Paris Elementary School.

Rusty also serves on the Board of Directors for the Travelers Rest Historical Society and serves on the School Improvement Committee at Paris Elementary School.

Outside Of King Law

Rusty is an active member of Taylors First Baptist Church in Taylors, South Carolina, where he is currently a deacon, serves on the finance committee and is first grade Sunday School teacher. He has also served on the safety team and as a youth basketball coach.

Rusty and his wife, Anna, have two children and reside in Greenville, South Carolina.

Eller - “Mike” was born in Columbia, SC, however, he moved to Abbeville, SC at an early age and considers Abbeville his “hometown.” Mike graduated from Abbeville High School and Presbyterian College in Clinton, SC. Mike enjoys playing golf, spending time with friends and cheering on the Gamecocks. Mike is married to Marisa, and they have two teenage sons, Jackson and Bennett.

Michael Ellis was raised in Conway, South Carolina. After graduating from Conway High School, Michael attended the University of South Carolina from which he graduated with a bachelor’s degree in economics.

After taking a year off, Michael attended the Charleston School of Law where he obtained his juris doctorate, leading ultimately to his admission to the South Carolina Bar in May of 2014.

Upon passing the bar, Michael practiced as an associate attorney at the same law firm he clerked with throughout law school. For nearly eight years, Michael handled a wide variety of cases including civil, criminal, probate, and family matters. Nearly 100% of Michael’s case load involved litigation.

While Michael very much enjoyed his wide variety of cases and the constant need to learn many areas of the law to advocate for his clients, he believed that he could best represent the South Carolina public by focusing on personal injury. Michael joined Derrick Law Firm Injury Lawyers in March of 2022.

Michael now resides with his wife, Allyson, in Summerville, South Carolina where he is kept very busy with his three children Emily, Madelyn, and Jack.

attorneys.name: Sloan P. Ellis
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Greenville, SC
attorneys.bio:
Along with his law partner Brandi Hinton, former federal prosecutor Sloan P. Ellis represents individuals and businesses in a wide variety of criminal and civil matters. He has extensive experience litigating in Federal and State courts in South Carolina. Having spent almost a decade in public service as a federal and state prosecutor, Sloan prosecuted thousands of cases from complex federal white collar crime, wire fraud, and money laundering to organized crime, gang and drug offenses, and violent crimes.

During Sloan’s time as a federal prosecutor, he worked hand in hand with numerous federal and state law enforcement agencies such as the FBI, DEA, IRS, Homeland Security, United States Postal Inspection Service, SLED, and the South Carolina Department of Revenue to investigate and prosecute white collar crime, violent crime, and drug offenses. Along with Brandi Hinton, Sloan prosecuted the fiftieth person in the United States to be charged with fraud in connection with the Paycheck Protection Program established under the CARES Act.

Sloan was the recipient of the 2020 United States Attorney’s award for excellence in prosecution. Before Sloan’s time as a federal prosecutor, he spent almost three years in private practice representing businesses and individuals just like he does today at Ellis Hinton. Sloan’s public service began at the Thirteenth Circuit Solicitor’s Office in Greenville, South Carolina. There, Sloan prosecuted thousands of state cases ranging from murder, burglary, and armed robbery to various drug-related and white collar crimes.

Before joining the Solicitor’s Office, Sloan was an attorney at the Nexsen Pruet law firm. Nexsen Pruet is a South Carolina-based firm that represents clients in virtually every industry in North and South Carolina and around the country. While at Nexsen Pruet, Sloan worked directly for William W. Wilkins, the former Chief Judge of the Fourth Circuit Court of Appeals and Chair of the Federal Sentencing Commission. At Nexsen Pruet, Sloan focused his practice on federal white collar criminal defense and complex civil litigation. He represented clients nationwide who were charged with or investigated for tax fraud, securities fraud, insider trading, health care fraud, violations of the False Claims Act, and various drug offenses. Sloan was also actively engaged in an appellate practice where he represented clients with appeals pending in the Fourth Circuit Court of Appeals, the South Carolina Supreme Court, and the South Carolina Court of Appeals.

Before joining Nexsen Pruet, Sloan worked in Charleston, South Carolina, with former United States Attorney E. Bart Daniel. While working with Mr. Daniel, Sloan focused on white collar criminal defense and was a member of the trial team who, during a month-long trial, defended the last person to be tried in what has been called the “largest and most complex white collar investigation in the history of South Carolina.”

Sloan is a ninth-generation South Carolinian who grew up on a farm in the small town of Due West. Working on the farm as a young man taught him the value of hard work and dedication to a cause. Sloan brings that work ethic and commitment to the clients that he represents and works every day to get them the best results possible.

Outside of work, Sloan serves on the Meyer Center for Special Children board of directors and is a member of First Presbyterian Church and the Haynsworth-Perry Inn of Court.

Jerry Evans, a mass torts attorney at RPWB, works to achieve justice on behalf of injured workers and others who have been wronged by corporate conduct.

He is an avid supporter of the performing arts and is a board member of the Charleston Symphony Orchestra. Evans also sits on the Board of Directors of American Voices, a non-profit cultural exchange that fosters the arts in conflict zones. He is married to Stephen Bajjaly.

attorneys.name: Colette Farhat
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Mt Pleasant, SC
attorneys.bio:
Colette Farhat is an associate attorney at Cavanaugh & Thickens, LLC, an award-winning South Carolina personal injury and workers’ compensation law firm. Since 2017, the firm has been recognized for its client-focused and results-driven approach and has recovered millions of dollars in compensation for clients across the state.

Colette joined the Cavanaugh & Thickens, LLC team in July of 2025 as the firm’s first injury attorney based full-time in our Charleston office, allowing us to broaden our impact and better serve the low country. She was drawn to our law firm for a few reasons: she had heard wonderful things about the firm’s culture and reputation, enjoyed how small and focused the firm is, and she wanted the opportunity to grow in her career as part of a tight-knit team that treats everyone like family.

Her journey to becoming an attorney was shaped by life-changing experiences. While in college, Colette had the opportunity to study abroad in South Africa, interning with a local defense attorney. That experience was unexpectedly cut short when her tour bus was hijacked and robbed at gunpoint, forcing her to return to the US and find another way to complete her senior project.

She ended up interning with a judge in Philadelphia, where she observed firsthand all the parts of the legal system at play. Those experiences solidified her decision to attend law school and pursue a career in advocacy.

Outside of work, Colette enjoys being outdoors, going to the beach or the gym, and spending time with her fiancé, his kids, and their dog.

attorneys.firm_name: Derrick Law Firm Injury Lawyers, PC
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Conway, SC
attorneys.bio:
R. Batten Farrar is a personal injury litigation attorney at the Derrick Law Firm Injury Lawyers in Greenville, SC. His practice is dedicated to the representation of those that have suffered significant harms and injuries. Batten has experience handling a wide-variety of significant and high-worth cases, involving permanent personal injuries, traumatic brain injuries, and wrongful death matters arising from automobile collisions, commercial truck and tow truck wrecks, animal attacks, and dangerous building conditions and hazards.

Prior to joining Derrick Law Firm Injury Lawyers, Batten handled insurance defense cases at two very well-respected regional defense firms. During that time, he became very familiar with how insurance companies evaluate and handle claims. He understands that trying to navigate the insurance claims process and legal system, especially while trying to heal from a significant harm or injury, is overwhelming and can be frustrating. He values the opportunity to counsel and advocate for his clients through these difficult events.

Batten grew up in Greenville, South Carolina, attending Sara Collins and Christ Church. He completed his undergraduate studies at the University of Georgia, where he met his now wife, and then attended the University of South Carolina School of Law. He has been recognized in Greenville Business Magazine’s annual “Legal Elite” awards from 2016-2023 (SC - Construction Defect and Construction Litigation) and as a Super Lawyers “Rising Star” from 2017-2021 (SC - Personal Injury). He serves on the Board of Directors for Fall for Greenville.

After graduating from Clemson University, Nick attended Wake Forest University where he earned his Master’s Degree in Religion with a focus on comparative religious ethics. After a friendly debate and a professor asking if he had considered law school, Nick enrolled in a graduated from the University of North Carolina – Chapel Hill School of Law in 2010.

Prior to joining Derrick Law Firm Injury Lawyers, Nick worked with two very well-respected regional defense firms, focusing primarily on insurance coverage and personal injury defense. Through that experience, Nick gained valuable insight into the insurance claims process and how to handle complex insurance coverage issues.

As a personal injury attorney at Derrick Law Firm Injury Lawyers, Nick utilizes his prior experience to zealously advocate for his clients. He understands how difficult and overwhelming navigating through insurance claims and the legal system can be and strives to help clients through every step of the process.

Nick is an experienced litigator, having handled numerous jury trials as well as cases before the SC Court of Appeals and SC Supreme Court. He has been consistently selected over the years by his peers for recognition of his professional achievements in both Greenville Business Magazine’s annual “Legal Elite” awards and in Super Lawyers as a “Rising Star” (2017-2021), and a “Super Lawyer” (2022-2024 Insurance Coverage).

attorneys.firm_name: Fayssoux & Landis Attorneys at Law, P.A.
attorneys.practice_type: Real Estate Transactions Lawyers in Greenville, SC
attorneys.bio:
Before founding Fayssoux & Landis Attorneys at Law, P.A., Jim was a senior partner in Anderson, Fayssoux and Chasteen, P.A. for over 30 years. Initially, Jim’s practice concentrated on domestic and family law, personal injury, and criminal prosecutorial work through the City of Greer, South Carolina. While he has now been practicing for almost 52 years he is still passionate about the practice and the people around him.

Since mid-1980 his practice has focused almost exclusively on real estate law. He handles both residential and commercial transactions and real estate litigation. For 3 decades Chicago Title has recognized Jim as a leading title agent.

Previously, Jim was an active member of the United States Army and the U.S. Army Reserve from 1972 to 1982.

Among many other commitments to local and civic organizations, he has volunteered with Meals on Wheels of Greenville for over 30 years by delivering meals to the homebound in our community, serving on the Board of Directors for Meals on Wheels of Greenville for several years. He is an active member of First Baptist Church, Greenville and has served on many committees.

Jim is married to Emily Grady Fayssoux and he has in addition to his son, Wally, a daughter who is employed by the School District of Greenville County who has 2 children, now in college.

attorneys.name: James (Wally) W. Fayssoux Jr.
attorneys.firm_name: Fayssoux & Landis Attorneys at Law, P.A.
attorneys.practice_type: Civil & Criminal Litigation Lawyers in Greenville, SC
attorneys.bio:
After graduating from The Citadel in 1996 with a BA in Business, Wally Fayssoux followed in his father’s footsteps and attended the University of South Carolina School of Law. He then returned home and fulfilled a dream by opening the Fayssoux Law Firm with his father. Wally has devoted most of his practice to representing plaintiffs in civil litigation. He has established a reputation as a passionate and dedicated trial lawyer. He has been successful in obtaining three of the top five largest personal injury verdicts in the history of the Greenville County state court system.

In recent years, he achieved the largest jury verdict in the state in 2012. Wally has tried numerous cases throughout the state and received multi-million dollar awards in three counties. His solid reputation expands statewide as he argues cases before the South Carolina Court of Appeals, the South Carolina Supreme Court, and the United States District Court.

Experience in Court

Wally has helped his clients achieve highly favorable results in personal injury cases involving defective products, medical malpractice, automobile accidents, trucking accidents, and other tort and business litigation. He has litigated numerous property rights cases, defending individual and corporate Plaintiffs against the Government in individual condemnation and other takings cases. Wally has also established a significant criminal practice and has represented numerous law enforcement officers in federal and state courts and numerous private citizens in actions ranging from driving offenses to capital punishment.

Although his efforts and reputation have secured numerous significant settlements for his clients, Wally is a zealous advocate of our jury system and has been lead counsel on over 75 jury trials. While the client will always dictate how a case is resolved, Wally continues to solidify his reputation as a passionate trial lawyer who is always willing to try his cases before a jury.

Wally Fayssoux is a lifelong resident of Greenville. He is married to Catherine O’Leary Fayssoux, a former prosecutor for Greenville County, and together they have two sons, Hammond and Beck.

attorneys.name: Jason Finley
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Mt Pleasant, SC
attorneys.bio:
Jason Finley was born and raised in Charleston, where he developed a strong work ethic and deep sense of community.

He proudly served in the United States Marine Corps, where he cultivated discipline, leadership, and a commitment to service—qualities that continue to shape his legal career. Following his military service, Jason spent 20 years in the construction industry, gaining firsthand knowledge of business operations, project management, and the challenges faced by working professionals and contractors.

After transitioning into the legal field, he served as an Assistant Prosecutor, where he built a reputation for integrity, thorough preparation, and effective advocacy in the courtroom. His prosecutorial experience provided him with a strong foundation in litigation and a comprehensive understanding of the justice system.

For the past year, Jason has been an attorney with Drennan Law Firm, where he continues to provide thoughtful and strategic legal counsel to his clients. His varied professional background allows him to connect with individuals from all walks of life and to approach each case with both legal insight and real-world perspective.

Outside of his professional work, Jason is a devoted husband, father, and avid outdoorsman. He and his wife are proud parents of two daughters and he values the time he spends with his family.

attorneys.name: Johnny Gasser
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Columbia, SC
attorneys.bio:
Johnny Gasser graduated Phi Betta Kappa receiving his Bachelor of Science degree in Criminal Justice from the University of South Carolina in 1984. He received his law degree from the University of South Carolina in 1987, graduating Cum Laude. Finishing in the top ten in his class earned Mr. Gasser membership in the South Carolina Chapter of The Order of the Coif.

Prosecution Background:

Johnny became an Assistant Solicitor in the Fifth Judicial Circuit in 1987 and in November 1993 was appointed Deputy Solicitor where he served in that position for nine years. In December 2002, he joined the staff at the United States Attorney's Office in Columbia as a Deputy Chief in charge of the Violent Crime Section. He was responsible for the supervision of twelve staff attorneys in the Columbia, Charleston, Florence and Greenville offices. On January 21, 2005, he was appointed Acting United States Attorney for the District of South Carolina and on August 16, 200S, he was sworn in as the United States Attorney for an interim term after receiving an executive appointment from Attorney General Alberto Gonzales. He served in that position until February 23, 2006, whereupon he returned as the Violent Crime Section Chief. He spent four years as a member of the Attorney General's Review Committee on Capital Cases in which he advised Attorney General John Ashcroft and Attorney General Gonzales on potential federal death penalty cases in the United States. On September 1, 2007, Johnny left government service and formed the Law Office of Harris & Gasser with his partner, Gregory P. Harris. The firm focuses primarily on federal and state criminal defense with an expanding personal injury and wrongful death civil practice, in which they work with other law firms.

Litigation Experience:

Johnny prosecuted thousands of criminal cases over his twenty-year career in the state and federal system, the largest percentage being violent felony offenders. He has handled over 150 jury trials, again most of which were violent felony cases. He has worked on approximately 400 homicide cases, to include in excess of 85 jury trials. He has prosecuted eight death penalty cases, including the United States Supreme Court's original case on "future dangerousness", Simmons v. South Carolina, as well as the first two federal death penalty cases in South Carolina history (United States v. Chadrick Fulks & United States v, Brandon Basham). Fulks and Basham were the first two defendants sentenced to death in the history of the Department of Justice where the victims' bodies were never recovered. Johnny was the first prosecutor in South Carolina to convict a man of raping his wife under the state's marital rape law; the first prosecutor in the state to successfully use Munchausen Syndrome by Proxy expert testimony in a child homicide case; and the first prosecutor in the nation to secure a homicide conviction in a crack cocaine fetus death.

Private Practice Experience:

Johnny Gasser has successfully represented doctors, lawyers, stock brokers, accountants, and business owners and executives in both state and federal court since entering private practice. He is a member of the South Carolina Bar, and is admitted to practice in the South Carolina Federal District Court and the Fourth Circuit Court of Appeals. Johnny emphasizes quality legal service above all else and he has unprecedented trial experience over the past thirty years. He evaluates the facts and circumstances of each case and then develops effective strategies to ensure that the client's best interests are protected. Johnny is routinely included in The Best Lawyers in America in the specialties of Criminal Defense: Non-White-Collar and Criminal Defense: White-Collar.

attorneys.name: Christopher James Geier
attorneys.firm_name: Christopher J. Geier, Attorney at Law, LLC
attorneys.practice_type: Traffic Tickets Lawyers in Beaufort, SC
attorneys.bio:
CHRISTOPHER J. GEIER, was born in Nurnberg, Germany, on January 5, 1973. As his father was a career United States Army Officer, Mr. Geier grew up all across the United States and Europe.

In 1995, Mr. Geier graduated from the University of Washington with a Bachelor of Arts in English. He was a member of the Phi Eta Sigma Honor Society and he was an officer in his fraternity, Psi Upsilon.

In May 2002, Mr. Geier graduated from Gonzaga University's School of Law in Spokane, Washington. During his years at Gonzaga, Mr. Geier clerked for a busy insurance defense litigation firm and he was elected President of the Connelly Chapter of Phi Alpha Delta.

In January 2023, after passing the Washington State Bar Examination, Mr. Geier joined the United States Army, working as a lawyer in the Judge Advocate General's Corps. After completing his Basic Course, Mr. Geier was stationed in Fort Stewart, Georgia with the 3rd Infantry Division. Mr. Geier spent his first year in the JAG Corps drafting wills and providing general legal advice to Soldiers and their family members. Mr. Geier was later stationed at Hunter Army Airfield, in Savannah, Georgia, where he served as the prosecutor and general counsel for the Garrison Commander and as the Officer-in-Charge of Hunter's Legal Office. Mr. Geier was also appointed as a Special Assistant to the United States Attorney. In June of 2005, Mr. Geier became the prosecuting attorney for the 3rd Infantry Division's Aviation Brigade and he deployed to Camp Taji, Iraq. After returning with the Division in 2006, Mr. Geier was appointed to serve as the general counsel for the Aviation Brigade Commander. After passing the South Carolina Bar Examination, Mr. Geier moved to Beaufort County in 2007. He spent three years in Bluffton, South Carolina with a well-established firm, focusing on criminal defense, driving under the influence cases and personal injury litigation.

In 2010, Mr. Geier opened his own law practice, in Beaufort, South Carolina. Mr. Geier is an active member of the South Carolina Bar Association and on inactive status in Washington State. He resides in Beaufort with his wife Amy, their two sons Riley and Carson, both of whom are students at Clemson University.

attorneys.firm_name: Fayssoux & Landis Attorneys at Law, P.A.
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Greenville, SC
attorneys.bio:
Geoff has been handling civil litigation matters ranging from motor vehicle accidents, trucking accidents, wrongful death cases, product liability cases, premises liability cases, construction defect cases, and insurance coverage disputes since becoming a member of the South Carolina Bar in 2007. For the first 14 years of his practice, before joining Fayssoux & Landis Attorneys at Law, P.A., Geoff worked for a large regional insurance defense firm where he was a partner and litigation team leader. Geoff’s extensive experience doing civil defense work brings a unique knowledge and understanding of how insurance companies evaluate and handle claims.

Geoff has successfully tried numerous cases throughout the Upstate of South Carolina. Geoff has also negotiated hundreds of successful settlements for clients of all types, including individuals, businesses, and insurance companies.

Greenville Business Magazine recognized Geoff as the Legal Elite of the Upstate in insurance and construction law from 2017 to 2021. From 2017 to 2019 and 2021, Geoff received the top attorney vote in construction law. The Legal Elite of the Upstate is voted on annually by active attorneys in Greenville.

Geoff was previously a Board Member of the South Carolina Defense Trial Attorneys Association from 2017 to 2021 and editor of their publication, The Defense Line. Geoff was also previously a member of the Federation for Defense and Corporate Counsel (“FDCC”). The FDCC is a prestigious invitation-only national association of the top defense and corporate counsel in the United States. Geoff is also a member of the American Board of Trial Advocates (“ABOTA”). ABOTA is an invitation-only national association of experienced trial attorneys and judges. ABOTA’s membership consists of more than 7,600 lawyers across the United States – equally balanced between plaintiff and defense.

Geoff was born and raised in Spartanburg, South Carolina. Geoff graduated from Auburn University in 2004. Geoff graduated from the University of South Carolina School of Law in 2007. Geoff is married to Kristen Gibbon of Spartanburg, South Carolina, and has three children, Sloane, Rett, and Cam.

When not practicing law, Geoff enjoys being with his family, cooking, working around the house, going to the beach, watching Auburn football, and playing golf.

attorneys.name: Steven E. Goldberg
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Lawyers in Summerville, SC
attorneys.bio:
Steven E. Goldberg joined the Steinberg Law Firm in 1993, following his father into a career of law. Steven explains, “Growing up, I was impressed to see my father working hard and the clients being truly thankful for that hard work.” Steven earned his bachelor’s degree from the University of Florida and his law degree from the University of South Carolina School of Law.

While practicing law for over 25 years, Steven has represented clients with on the job injuries and automobile wrecks. He has had successful trial appearances as well as settlements totaling over several million dollars. Over the past several years, Steven has increased his practice to represent families of those who have had loved ones injured or killed in nursing homes because of neglect.

Steven maintains his office in Summerville, South Carolina but practices law at both the Broad Street and Goose Creek locations. He is very active in the legal community, having served as President of the South Carolina Injured Workers’ Advocates and Chairperson of the South Carolina Bar Worker’s Compensation Section. He has also served on the board of Governors for the Association for Justice (Trial Lawyers).

Steven has argued Workers’ Compensation cases before the South Carolina Court of Appeals and the South Carolina Supreme Court. He also addresses colleagues and members of the business community at various seminars regarding Workers Compensation issues.

He is a member of KKBE and has served as President of the East Cooper Jewish Community and as Chairman for Operation Home, an organization devoted to making homes safer for lower income residents. He also is active with the Coastal Community Foundation, serving as chair for the Grantmaking and Leadership Committee.

attorneys.name: Adam P. Greene
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Lawyers in Goose Creek, SC
attorneys.bio:
Adam Greene serves as a partner at Steinberg Law Firm, dedicating his practice to workers’ compensation, longshore and harbor workers’ injury claims, and Social Security disability cases. Over the years, he has guided hundreds of injured workers through complex legal challenges and achieved multimillion-dollar results on their behalf.

Earlier in his career, Adam represented insurance carriers and employers in workplace injury litigation. That defense-side experience sharpened his understanding of how benefits are contested and what strategies are used to limit exposure. He now leverages that insight to anticipate defenses, build stronger claims, and safeguard his clients’ rights.

Having grown up in a South Carolina community rooted in textile and industrial work, Adam understands the ripple effect a serious injury can have on a family. Those experiences inspired his commitment to standing alongside injured workers as they seek medical treatment, wage replacement, and long-term security.

A graduate of the University of South Carolina School of Law, Adam has been repeatedly recognized in editions of South Carolina Business Magazine’s Legal Elite. He was also selected for 40 Under 40 by The National Trial Lawyers and Best Lawyers: Ones to Watch.

Outside the office, Adam enjoys hunting and fishing, as well as relaxing at home with his wife, their two sons, and their dog, Judge.

attorneys.name: Taylor L. Grooms
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Charleston, SC
attorneys.bio:
Taylor L. Grooms has dedicated his life to fighting for those who have been injured or killed by the negligence of others. He is committed to seeing his clients properly compensated for their injuries. Taylor was recently inducted into the Million Dollar Advocates Forum, and he also recently finished serving a two-year term as President of the Berkeley County Bar Association. He is a graduate of Leadership Berkeley, and serves on the Board of the Bradley Blake Foundation.

Taylor has won the AVVO Client’s Choice Award for the past four years for providing excellent customer service. He has also been named to Super Lawyers “Rising Stars” list, the Best Lawyers “Ones to Watch” List, and the National Trial Lawyers Association “Top 40 Under 40.”

Taylor was born and raised in Bonneau, South Carolina, and is an Honors Graduate of Timberland High School. He went on to graduate from Clemson University, and then attended the University of South Carolina School of Law. He was a 5-time Dean’s List recipient at USC Law, and he graduated with Cum Laude honors.

After law school, Taylor clerked for Judge Roger M. Young, Sr., who was the Chief Judge for the Ninth Circuit (Charleston and Berkeley County) and Fourteenth Circuit (Hampton, Colleton, Allendale, Jasper, and Beaufort County). He spent the next six years practicing law at a large Lowcountry personal injury and workers' compensation firm. When not in the office, Taylor enjoys boating and trying new restaurants with his family.

attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Gaffney, SC
attorneys.bio:
Jordan Guthrie is a Partner in Spartanburg, South Carolina and works out of the firm’s Spartanburg and Gaffney offices. Jordan primary practice of law is in the area of criminal law. He also serves as the Chair of the firm’s Criminal Law Practice Area Group.

Jordan received his B.A. in Political Science from the University of North Carolina at Wilmington and later earned a J.D. at the Charleston School of Law. While in law school, Jordan was president of the Historical Preservation Society and worked to keep noteworthy historical homes and buildings intact during Charleston’s ongoing expansion. Clerking for a small firm in Summerville, SC, Jordan learned the importance of client relations while practicing in a tight knit Carolina community.

Originally from New Bern, NC, Jordan now lives in Moore, SC with his wife, daughter, and two labs. In his free time he enjoys spending time with his family, camping, and highland games competition.

attorneys.name: Casey Hall
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Mt. Pleasant, SC
attorneys.bio:
Originally from the small town of Arcadia, Florida, Casey F. Hall graduated from Florida State University in 2018, where she earned a Bachelor of Arts and Sciences degree in Humanities. She moved from the Sunshine State to South Carolina, where she obtained her law degree at Charleston School of Law. During her studies, Ms. Hall completed her internship with the Florida State Attorney’s Office in Manatee County and was proudly a member of the Children & Family Law Society as well as the Phi Delta Phi Honor Society.

Upon Admission to the South Carolina Bar in the Fall of 2023 and joining the Charleston County Bar, Ms. Hall also sat for the Florida Bar in the Spring of 2024 and was admitted to the Florida Bar in May of 2024.

As a fourth-generation attorney and cattle rancher, Ms. Hall’s upbringing has given her a deep appreciation for hard work, community, and resilience. With her strong work ethic and passion to help support and empower others, she understands advocating for her clients and prioritizing what is most important to them, especially in the difficult and stressful times of their lives.

She has been working in the field of family law since 2024, focusing on matters including divorce, child custody, child support, post-decree modifications, and adoptions. In 2025, she joins Bluestein & Douglas LLC, where she continues to provide compassionate and practical legal counsel, guiding clients through the legal process as they navigate significant life transitions.

Outside of work, Ms. Hall enjoys discovering new places, spending quality time with her family and friends, tending to her garden, and lending a hand at her family’s cattle ranch.

attorneys.name: Ken W. Harrell
attorneys.practice_type: Business Operations Lawyers in North Charleston, SC
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Harrell, born in 1963 in Waverly, Virginia, spent his first six years as a lawyer with Nelson, Mullins, Riley and Scarborough, a respected South Carolina corporate defense law firm. But in 1994 when he joined the Joye Law Firm, he switched his focus to helping individuals in cases involving workers' compensation claims and defective products. Mr. Harrell heads up the firm's workers' compensation and mass torts practices.

Mr. Harrell is a frequent author and speaker for the South Carolina Bar's Continuing Legal Education Program. Among the programs where he has been a featured speaker are "The Law of Workers' Compensation in South Carolina," "Trying the Automobile Injury Case," "Paralegals and the Litigation Team in South Carolina," and "Premises Liability: Preparation and Trial of a Difficult Case in South Carolina."

Active in legal and civic organizations, Mr. Harrell serves as a board member of the William and Mary Law School Association and ad sales chairman for the Rotary/Red Cross high school basketball tournament in North Charleston. He also has served as a pack leader for the Christ Our King Cub Scouts Pack 470 and as a Little League coach for the Mount Pleasant Recreation Department.

Mr. Harrell and his wife, Jeannie, have three children - two sons and a daughter. His recreational interests include Civil War history, softball, kayaking, South Carolina Gamecocks football and NASCAR.

attorneys.name: Heather A. Hartoin
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Litigation Lawyers in Summerville, SC
attorneys.bio:
Heather A. Hartoin is an experienced trial attorney who focuses her practice on personal injury litigation and criminal defense. Prior to joining John Price Law Firm, LLC in 2011, she worked for Allstate Insurance Company in the Indianapolis Staff Counsel Office, where she defended both first-party and third-party liability claims and prosecuted subrogation actions on behalf of the company. She began her legal career as a Deputy Prosecuting Attorney in Tippecanoe County, Indiana, concentrating her practice in the area of criminal domestic violence. In addition to practicing law, she is an Adjunct Professor of Law at the Charleston School of Law, where she has taught criminal law.

Heather obtained her Juris Doctorate degree, with a Criminal Law Concentration, from Valparaiso University School of Law in 2002, where she received honors for her participation in both the National Mock Trial Team and the Criminal Law Clinic. She also obtained her undergraduate degree from Valparaiso University, where she graduated Cum Laude in 1999 with a Bachelor of Arts degree, majoring in Psychology and Pre-Physical Therapy.

Heather is admitted to practice law in the states of South Carolina and Indiana, and the United States District Court for the Northern District of Indiana.

Heather lives in Summerville with her husband, Steve, and their three dogs.

attorneys.name: Brian J. Headley
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice Lawyers in Daniel Island, SC
attorneys.bio:
Brian J. Headley has been a practicing litigator since 2004 and has a wealth of experience in all types of civil litigation. Prior to starting his own practice in 2012, Brian had worked at three civil litigation defense firms in Charleston, West Virginia, and Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. Over the years, Brian has litigated a wide variety of commercial litigation, insurance coverage, bad faith, employment, product liability, construction, toxic tort, wrongful death, and personal injury actions. In 2012, Brian moved to Charleston, South Carolina, and founded the firm that has become Headley Law Firm LLC. Since that time, Brian has focused largely on representing victims of medical malpractice and other individuals who have sustained serious injuries through no fault of their own. Headley Law Firm LLC has been fortunate to grow rapidly since 2017 in large part as a result of referrals from other lawyers who are familiar with the firm's capabilities. Headley Law Firm LLC has become the law firm that lawyers call when they or their clients need help.

Brian received his J.D. degree in 2004 from the West Virginia University College of Law where he was a member of the West Virginia Law Review, Order of the Coif, and finished fourth in his graduating class. He also served as a law clerk to the Honorable Robert B. King of the United States Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit during his final semester of law school. Brian received his undergraduate degree from West Virginia University in 2001, graduated summa cum laude, and received but a single ‘B' during his undergraduate studies (in Jazz of all subjects).

Brian is licensed to practice in South Carolina, West Virginia, Pennsylvania, Kentucky, Ohio, and Virginia, as well as the United States District Courts for the District of South Carolina, the Northern and Southern Districts of West Virginia, and the Western District of Pennsylvania. Brian resides on Daniel Island with his wife, Kelly, and they have two young children, Alex and Jackson. Mr. Headley is a member of St. Clare of Assisi Catholic Church on Daniel Island.

attorneys.bio:
George M. Hearn, Jr. was born in Charlotte, NC in 1951, the son of George and Martha Hearn.He grew up in Rock Hill, SC where he graduated from Rock Hill High School in 1970. In 1974, he receieved a B.A. degree in economics from Duke University and his J.D. from the University of South Carolina School of Law in 1977.

George was admitted to the South Carolina Bar in 1977 and served as a clerk to The Honorable Chief Justice J. Woodrow Lewis of the South Carolina Supreme Court from 1977 to 1979. He served as a member of the Board of Commissioners on Grievances and Discipline from 1983 until 1985 and was a member of the Executive Board from 1985 to 1986. In 1986, he became a member of the South Carolina Board of Bar Examiners and has been Chairman of that Board since 1997. George has been a speaker at numerous judicial and continuing legal education seminars throughout the state. In 1999, he received the Gold Compleat Lawyer Award from the South Carolina Bar. He is admitted to practice in both state and federal courts, with a focus on personal injury, product liability, domestic relations, and appelate law.

A formidable trial attorney, he specializes in the areas of wrongful death, personal injury, workers' compensation and products liability.

attorneys.name: J. Ryan Heiskell
attorneys.practice_type: Automotive Safety - Product Liability Lawyers in Georgetown, SC
attorneys.bio:
"Our firm is a big family; we all have our lives invested in it. Each new client becomes a part of that and enjoys all of the benefits of the strong, united force that is the Bell Legal Group..."

While having just graduated law school in 2007, J. Ryan Heiskell has years of first-hand knowledge and experience with the law and particularly with products liability litigation. After obtaining his undergraduate degree from DePaul University in Chicago, IL, Ryan sought to attend medical school in Virginia. After moving there with his wife and while waiting out his year to establish residency, he began working for his father at the Michie, Hamlett law firm in Charlottesville, VA. Ryan's father had been trying cases against Ford Motor Company and other manufacturers for years and needed help with a new case, a sudden acceleration case involving the death of a 13-year-old child.

After two years of discovery battles, millions of pages of document production and countless hours of legal research, Ryan decided he didn't want to go to medical school any longer; he wanted to be a trial lawyer. That case was Huber v. Ford and was tried to a multi-million dollar Plaintiffs' verdict.

In 2004, Ryan moved his wife and 8-month-old son to Ada, OH to attend law school at the Ohio Northern University. Following his second year of school and a second baby boy, he received a phone-call from Ed Bell in Georgetown, SC, who had heard about Ryan's work on sudden acceleration cases and asked for his help in preparing for an upcoming trial. Ryan spent the summer with Ed's team, working day and night arming for battle. That case, Watson v. Ford, was also tried to a verdict, and Plaintiffs were awarded $18 Million Dollars. Ryan returned to Ohio and completed his final year of law school.

Since then, Ryan and his family (3 sons) have permanently moved to Pawleys Island, SC, where he enjoys his role as the leader of the firm's automotive safety/ product liability division. He manages cases across the country against Ford, GM, Chrysler, Toyota, Kia, and Nissan, which involve defects in the following areas: sudden acceleration, handling and stability, roof crush, general occupant protection, seatbelt spool-out and inertial buckle unlatch, door latch/lock mechanism, seatback failure, seat-track failure, folding seat release mechanism failure, airbags, window glazing, park-to-reverse, brake system failures, warnings, general malfunction, and speed control deactivation switch fires.

attorneys.name: Brandi B. Hinton
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Greenville, SC
attorneys.bio:
Brandi Hinton is a former federal and state prosecutor who has handled thousands of criminal cases both as a prosecutor and as a defense attorney. A Columbia, South Carolina native and a graduate of the University of South Carolina, Brandi attended law school at the Charleston School of Law, where she was a member of the Moot Court Board, Student Trial Lawyers Association, Phi Delta Phi, Orientation Committee, Academic Support Search Committee, James L. Pettigru Inn of Court, and served on the Alumni Association Board. Upon graduation from law school, she was chosen as a member of the Charleston School of Law Forensic Club.

After graduating from law school, Brandi clerked for the Honorable Mikell R. Scarborough during the height of the foreclosure crisis in Charleston County. She then worked in the Thirteenth Circuit Solicitor’s Office in both Greenville and Pickens counties for eight years, where she handled thousands of cases and tried over twenty-five cases, including murder, criminal sexual conduct, armed robbery, burglary, domestic violence, white collar, drug trafficking, and bank robbery.

Brandi, along with her partner Sloan Ellis, was an Assistant United States Attorney in the United States Attorney’s Office for the District of South Carolina. As a federal prosecutor, she was assigned to the Organized Crime Drug Enforcement Task Force, where she prosecuted large-scale drug trafficking crimes. She also prosecuted complex white collar crimes such as wire fraud, money laundering, and PPP fraud in addition to racketeering (RICO), violent crimes in aid of racketeering (VICAR), bank robbery, and Hobbs Act robbery cases. Brandi was part of the team of prosecutors who prosecuted the largest federal racketeering conspiracy in South Carolina's history. Brandi was the recipient of the 2021 United States Attorney’s award for excellence in prosecution.

Outside of work, Brandi serves on the Julie Valentine Center Board of Directors and is a member of the Haynsworth-Perry Inn of Court.

Awards and Honors

Honors

2021 United States Attorney’s award for excellence in prosecution.

attorneys.name: AJ Holloway
attorneys.firm_name: Derrick Law Firm Injury Lawyers, PC
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Conway, SC
attorneys.bio:
AJ Holloway was born and raised in the Myrtle Beach area. He attended Socastee High School where he earned an International Baccalaureate Diploma. He then went on to Clemson University and graduated magna cum laude. After Clemson, he attended the University of South Carolina School of Law where he was a member of the Moot Court Bar and involved in various community service and mentoring groups. AJ has continued to be involved in many community service activities throughout his legal career including participating in the Make-A-Wish Trailblaze Challenge.

He began his legal career with the defense firm of Gallivan, White & Boyd in Columbia, SC. After several years of defending large companies, he then pursued his desire to represent plaintiffs rather than companies and joined Richardson, Patrick, Westbrook & Brickman’s Columbia office. AJ’s prior experience with a defense firm provides insight into how companies approach lawsuits filed against them. AJ gained experience with these prior firms and is excited to return to Horry County to work on behalf of individuals who have been injured through no fault of their own. His areas of practice include car accidents, catastrophic injuries, and premises liability.

In April 2020, AJ was confirmed by the SC Legislature as a Commissioner on the State Ethics Commission for the term of 2020 to 2025. The Ethics Commission conducts investigations in response to complaints filed against members and candidates of the General Assembly as well as those filed against elected and appointed state and local public officials.

If you have been injured, AJ and the rest of Derrick Law Firm Injury Lawyers team are ready to help.

attorneys.name: S. Randall Hood
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Rock Hill, SC
attorneys.bio:
RANDALL ("RANDY") HOOD focuses his practice on representing individuals who have been catastrophically injured in a preventable accident or representing persons who have been wronged by an act of a corporation on a large scale basis. His catastrophic injury practice includes persons injured in a medical malpractice case, nursing home abuse/neglect situation, product liability case, tractor trailer collision, or some other serious incident. The catastrophic injuries suffered by some of his clients have included brain injury, burn injury, paralysis, amputation, cerebral palsy and death. Randall also represents persons who have suffered some type of injury due to wrongful conduct on behalf of a corporation or organized entity. This type of situation presents an opportunity for Randall to represent a class of individuals (Class Action) or many individual claims in a consolidated action against corporate entities (Multi District Litigation or MDL).

Randall was born in Macon Georgia and moved to Charlotte North Carolina when he was 12 years old. He attended public schools in Charlotte, North Carolina and attended college at the local University in Charlotte, North Carolina (University of North Carolina at Charlotte). attorneys.name: Josh Hudson
attorneys.practice_type: Trustee Litigation Lawyers in Greenville, SC
attorneys.bio:
Josh is an experienced litigator who has been in practice since 2006. Josh handles trustee and creditor litigation in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court and represents corporate clients and lenders in disputes that involve breach of contracts or collections. He also represents individuals in real estate litigation, personal injury litigation, and general civil litigation.

Before moving to Greenville, his wife’s hometown, Josh cut his teeth with five years in a small-town general practice in his hometown of Danville, Kentucky. This general practice foundation in a variety of disciplines allowed Josh to gain experience in numerous areas of dispute resolution and transactional work, and gave him the right blend of skills and responsiveness needed to adeptly practice in various areas of the law.

Josh has been recognized multiple times by his peers for his outstanding work and commitment to the spirit of the legal profession, including being named one of the Upstate’s Legal Elite in Greenville Business Magazine every year since 2017, and being honored as the top vote recipient for Bankruptcy and Creditor’s Rights in 2021. His knowledge of the law, professional work ethic, and advocacy on behalf of clients has made him a trusted advisor for both individuals and businesses alike.

Josh has always been active in trade associations and civic boards. In addition to his activities with professional organizations, he is committed to the community in which he lives and works. When not in the office or courtroom, Josh enjoys spending time with his wife, Erin, and their three children, and rooting for the Kentucky Wildcats. He and his family are active members of Christ Church Episcopal.

attorneys.name: Theodore H. Huge
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Charleston, SC
attorneys.bio:
Theodore ("Ted") Huge is a seasoned civil litigation and transactional attorney. For over 15 years, he has represented clients involved in contract disputes, class action representatives, False Claims Act Realtors and persons injured by exposure to asbestos and other toxic substances. He has extensive experience in securities litigation and transactions and products liability and civil racketeering cases. Mr. Huge maintains a transactional law practice and represents several small and medium-sized businesses in South Carolina. He is also a member of and general counsel for a large college scholarship foundation. He has been recognized for his excellent writing, negotiation and communication skills and proven track record for providing superior, personalized, cost-effective representation to his clients.

Mr. Huge earned his Juris Doctor degree at Georgetown University and graduated from Duke University with Bachelor of Arts degrees in Public Policy and Mathematics. He is licensed to practice law in Virginia, South Carolina, the U.S. Virgin Islands and the District of Columbia. Prior to joining forces with Stephen Harris in 2010, Mr. Huge gained several years' experience working for large litigation firms and spent two years as a financial analyst for an investment fund and a large retail franchisee. Mr. Huge devotes his free time to volunteer work, participation in sports leagues and playing lead guitar with a local rock band.

attorneys.name: Francis Humphries
attorneys.firm_name: Monckton Hembree Humphries Attorneys At Law
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Myrtle Beach, SC
attorneys.bio:
I graduated from the University of South Carolina School of Law in 1989. After serving one year as law clerk to the Honorable Randall T. Bell at the South Carolina Court of Appeals, I began my career in prosecution.

From 1990 to 1993, I served as an assistant solicitor in the Ninth Circuit (Berkeley County) on the Drug Strike Force where I prosecuted drug and drug related violent offenses. In 1993 through 1999, I prosecuted in the Eleventh Circuit (Lexington County) beginning as an assistant solicitor and then deputy solicitor for the circuit.

In 1999, I moved to Conway, South Carolina and I accepted the appointment of Deputy Solicitor for the Fifteenth Circuit (Horry and Georgetown Counties) where I served until December of 2009. In my career, I have successfully prosecuted over 100 murder cases including over 20 capital murder cases, many of which have been covered by national media. My focus over the last fifteen years was complex and major case litigation.

In January of 2010 after twenty years as a prosecutor, I entered private practice with the Monckton Law Firm focusing on criminal law and personal injury including wrongful death with a strong emphasis on litigation.

attorneys.name: Sarah Hurley
attorneys.practice_type: Business & Commercial Law Lawyers in Greenville, SC
attorneys.bio:
Sarah practiced law in Washington, D.C. and Atlanta before returning to her hometown of Greenville, South Carolina in 1998. From 1999 to 2006 she was in the Business Litigation practice group of Womble Carlyle Sandridge & Rice (now Womble Bond Dickinson) and from 2008 to 2019 was in the Business Litigation practice group of Turner Padget Graham & Laney. In 2006, she chose to take a sabbatical from the practice of law and opened "Brew & Ewe", which was an upscale retail and coffee/sandwich shop located in downtown Greenville. She owned and managed Brew & Ewe until 2016. Owning and operating Brew & Ewe was the fulfillment of a life dream to have her own small retail business.

In October 2019, she pursued her other dream of starting her own law firm. With her husband, Tim Hurley, they opened Hurley Law PA, and have not looked back!

Sarah has successfully tried jury cases to a verdict in all levels of trial courts in South Carolina, including Federal Court. She has been counsel in more than 200 cases in the United States District Court for South Carolina, and hundreds more in the State courts.

Sarah is also a certified mediator and enjoys the opportunity to help parties resolve their conflicts. When her schedule permits, Sarah serves as a volunteer mediator with the Upstate Mediation Center.

Brandon Hylton was born and raised in the Pee Dee area of South Carolina and is a native of Kingstree, SC. He attended Williamsburg Academy, and then went on to Presbyterian College. After PC, he attended the University of South Carolina School of Law. While in law school, Brandon was presented with the Sol Siegal Award for his academic achievement.

Prior to Derrick Law Firm Injury Lawyers, Brandon was a member of the defense firm of McAngus Goudelock and Courie. After years of defending insurance companies, he then pursued his desire to represent injured workers. Brandon’s practice focuses mainly on workers' compensation, as he has over 20 years of experience practicing in the South Carolina Workers' Compensation system.

attorneys.name: Brian C. Johnson
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Lawyers in Mt. Pleasant, SC
attorneys.bio:
Attending the College of Charleston on a full athletic scholarship, Brian received his Bachelor of Arts degree from the College of Charleston in 1994. Upon graduation, Brian worked as a financial advisor with John Hancock Financial Services in Mt. Pleasant. In 1997, Brian started law school and in 2000, received his Juris Doctor from the University of South Carolina School of Law. After graduation, Brian was appointed as an Assistant Attorney General by South Carolina Attorney General Charlie Condon. During this time, Brian prosecuted a wide range of criminal charges including murder, drug trafficking, drug possession, gun charges, elder abuse, criminal domestic violence, driving under the influence and environmental issues. He served on the Criminal Domestic Task Force as well. A native of Charleston, Brian returned home in 2002, working with both Finkel & Altman and the Clekis Law Firm.

In 2006, Brian and longtime friend, Ryan Bluestein, formed Bluestein & Johnson, LLC. Brian focuses his practice primarily on Worker's Compensation, Personal Injury, Criminal Defense, and Domestic. Brian has successfully handled and tried various workers compensation cases including permanent and total cases. He has tried numerous personal injury cases, prevailing and receiving great results for his injured clients. Brian's experience as a prosecutor has helped him reach successful resolutions for his criminal clients, from negotiating a plea all the way to trying the case in the courtroom. Brian has effectively dealt with a wide range of domestic cases including divorces, child custody issues, termination of parental rights and adoption cases.

Active in the Charleston community, he attends many events and is a member of Providence Baptist Church. He serves as an adjunct professor at Southern Wesleyan University and teaches various legal classes. He is a member of the Charleston County Bar and the South Carolina Trial Lawyers Association.

attorneys.name: Nancy E. Johnson
attorneys.practice_type: Bankruptcy Law Lawyers in Columbia, SC
attorneys.bio:
Nancy was born in Greenville, Tennessee, in 1966. She first attended college at East Tennessee State University in Johnson City, Tennessee but moved to Myrtle Beach, South Carolina after her Sophomore year. There she attended the University of South Carolina-Coastal Carolina College, studying history and graduating magna cum laude in 1991.

In 1993, she moved to Columbia, South Carolina, where she attended the University of South Carolina School of Law. She was a member of the South Carolina Law Review, the Order of Wig and Robe, the Order of the Coif, and was a legal writing instructor. She graduated cum laude in 1996 and was admitted to practice law in South Carolina in 1996 and in North Carolina in 1997.

Nancy began her professional career clerking for the Honorable Samuel H. Stilwell, judge of the South Carolina Court of Appeals. She practices in the area of bankruptcy law, representing both creditors and debtors in both consumer and commercial settings.

attorneys.firm_name: Law Office of Darrell Thomas Johnson, Jr., LLC
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury - Plaintiff Lawyers in Hardeeville, SC
attorneys.bio:
Warren Johnson is a native of Hardeeville, S.C. After graduation from the University of South Carolina in 2000, he attended the University of South Carolina School of Law. Warren received his law degree and decided to return to Hardeeville to join his father's firm in 2003. Warren handles general litigation but his primary focus is personal injury and workers compensation cases. In addition, Warren has been actively involved in helping injured workers from the Savannah River Site seek benefits under the EEOICPA and South Carolina Workers Compensation Act since 2011. His firm, along with attorney Bob Warren of Asheville, NC, has spent thousands of hours helping workers with devastating health conditions resulting from their work around toxic and/or radioactive materials seek compensation and medical care.

Warren is married to Kristen Cook Johnson and the proud father of twin daughters, Madeline and Amelia Johnson. He is the Town Attorney for the Town of Ridgeland, former member of the Jasper County Board of Elections and Voter Registration, former Vice Chairman of the Jasper County Board of Disabilities and Special Needs, former member of the Board of Governors for the Coastal Carolina Hospital in Hardeeville, and Magistrate Judge for Jasper County.
