attorneys.name: Christopher A. Wellborn
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Rock Hill, SC
attorneys.bio:
Rock Hill Criminal Defense Law Firm

Located in Rock Hill, South Carolina, Christopher A. Wellborn, P.A., is the only law firm in the area that devotes 100% of its practice to criminal defense. No matter the nature of your criminal charge, including DUI, drug charges, robbery, child abuse, or juvenile delinquency, contact the firm for a free initial consultation.

Attorney Christopher A. Wellborn, earned his law degree in 1988 from the University of San Diego School of Law after receiving a bachelor of arts from Bates College in Lewiston, Maine. A long-time resident of South Carolina, Wellborn is committed to serving the people of his area.

Christopher A. Wellborn is the current president of the National Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers and has served on the board of directors and executive committee of The National Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers. He is also a founding member and past President of the South Carolina Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers and is a past President of the York County Bar Association, and is active in the South Carolina Bar Association. He is a frequent speaker at seminars on Criminal Law topics both on a state and national level.

Former York County Prosecutor

Before opening his criminal defense law firm in 1997, Christopher A. Wellborn worked extensively in criminal law, including serving as prosecutor for York County. There, he prosecuted a whole range of crimes, from DUI to burglary to murder. This experience as a prosecutor gives him unusual insight into the criminal justice system, which he uses on behalf of criminal defendants.

Thirty years after graduating from law school, Attorney Christopher A. Wellborn currently handles cases throughout South Carolina in state, federal, juvenile, and magistrate courts. He is the only attorney in the area, outside of public defenders, who devotes his entire practice to criminal defense.

Attorney Christopher A. Wellborn is deeply rooted within the community he serves. He speaks frequently at seminars, discussing criminal defense topics. A founding member and former president of South Carolina Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, he is well-known and respected by area judges, lawyers, court staff, police officials, counselors, therapists, and other professionals. He belongs to the York County Bar Association, the South Carolina Bar Association, and the National Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers.

Christopher A. Wellborn is a recipient of the Champion of Justice Legal Award bestowed by the National Association of Criminal Defense Attorneys.

attorneys.name: Burns Wetmore
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal and Traffic Defense Lawyers in Charleston, SC
attorneys.bio:
Burns is a former federal, state and municipal prosecutor, practicing criminal law since 1998. In addition to his practice with the Wetmore Law Firm, he also serves as a Municipal Judge for the City of Folly Beach. Throughout his career, and from all perspectives of the judicial system, he has earned an outstanding reputation with law enforcement, prosecution and the judiciary. Trust him to put his experience and relationships to work for you in your time of need.

He began his legal career as the City of Charleston’s chief jury trial prosecutor. There he handled all manner of misdemeanor crimes, Driving Under the Influence charges and traffic violations.

He then served as an Assistant Solicitor for the Ninth Judicial Circuit in both Charleston and Berkeley Counties, acting as a managing litigation team leader and the chief drug prosecutor. Over a long tenure, he took the lead in countless felonies: Murder and other violent crime, Trafficking and other drug offenses, Burglary and other property crime and Felony Driving Under the Influence and other serious traffic charges.

He then served as an Assistant United States Attorney in Charleston, South Carolina. Assigned to the Violent Crime section, he represented the United States in Drug Trafficking, Gang Intervention and Firearms investigations. He also served as the chief prosecutor for the Central Violations Bureau, where he handled all manner of misdemeanor violations of federal law.

In 2023, he was appointed Municipal Judge for the City of Folly Beach. From the bench, he continues to serve the public, presiding over cases involving Driving Under the Influence and other alcohol offenses, drug offenses and other violations of state law and city code.Burns joined his wife, Spencer, at the Wetmore Law Firm. His practice focuses on seeking justice for those who have been injured by the actions of others or who have been victimized by crime. Being charged with a crime is often the darkest hour for you and your family. Burns is experienced and highly skilled at criminal and traffic defense, to include violent crime, drug offenses and Driving Under the Influence and other alcohol and traffic violations. He is always available to serve his clients in their time of need. Outside of work, the Wetmores enjoy time with their daughters and dogs on the water at their home on Folly Beach, South Carolina.

attorneys.name: Thomas M. White
attorneys.practice_type: Work injury Lawyers in Goose Creek, SC
attorneys.bio:
Tom White grew up in the textile-producing Upstate of South Carolina working third shift in the cotton mills.That experience shaped his desire to help working people.

He graduated from the University of Virginia with distinction, he then graduated in the top of his class at the South Carolina School of Law in 1977 and was admitted to the SC Bar in 1978. Tom began his law career as a public defender and joined the Steinberg Law Firm in 1980. He is a member of the Charleston County Bar Association, the South Carolina Bar Association and the South Carolina Trial Lawyers Association. For the past twenty years, Tom has been listed in Best Lawyers in America and Super Lawyers For Workers’ Compensation. Tom exclusively handles work injury cases with many cases paid to the injured workers in excess of a million dollars.

Tom has served on the Charleston County Common Pleas Liaison Committee and the Charleston County Grievance Committee. He is a former municipal judge in Goose Creek

and is a member of the South Carolina Workers’ Compensation Claimants’ Association.

Tom lives in Charleston with his wife and has three children and three grandchildren.

attorneys.name: Jamie Williams
attorneys.firm_name: Derrick Law Firm Injury Lawyers, PC
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Conway, SC
attorneys.bio:
Jamie Williams is personal injury and construction defect litigation attorney in our Columbia, SC office. Jamie was born and raised in Columbia. He graduated from Dreher High School, Presbyterian College, and the University of South Carolina School of Law. In law school, Jamie was on the Dean’s List every semester and was inducted into the Order of the Wig and Robe.

Jamie brings a different perspective in the representation of his clients having worked in the South Carolina legal community for over 17 years in various roles ranging from file clerk to partner of a defense firm. He began his career as an attorney representing large financial institutions in the court room and eventually began defending individuals and businesses through their insurance companies in construction defect and personal injury litigation. These experiences provided him with invaluable knowledge on how insurance companies handle and value claims and lawsuits. Before joining Derrick Law Firm Injury Lawyers, Jamie was a partner at a well-respected defense firm where he defended businesses involved in high value multi-party litigation cases. He left his partnership to bring his courtroom experience to the plaintiffs’ side so he could zealously advocate for those that do not have the backing of large insurance companies.

Outside of work, Jamie spends all the time he can with his wife, Meredith, and two young boys, Hayes and Monte. He loves coaching and cheering for his boys’ sports teams. The family also enjoys Gamecock sports. They frequently attend Carolina football, baseball, men’s basketball and women’s basketball games.

attorneys.name: Kathryn Williams
attorneys.practice_type: Workers' Compensation Lawyers in Greenville, SC
attorneys.bio:
Kathryn Williams has served residents of the greater Greenville area and the surrounding counties of Upstate South Carolina since 1983. She is known as a tenacious fighter representing injured workers in Workers’ Compensation claims. Kathryn has been listed in "Best Lawyers in America" in the practice area of Workers' Compensation in South Carolina every year since 2007.

She has practiced law for thirty years and has a stellar reputation as a compassionate and aggressive advocate. Because she has spent countless hours in the courtroom fighting for those injured on the job, it is no wonder her name has appeared in several reported cases, influencing the development of her chosen practice area.

Ms. Williams’ expansive network of legal colleagues play a part in her success and the positive results she garners for her clients. As well as being a Past President of the South Carolina Association for Justice, she was President of the Association of South Carolina Claimant Attorneys for Workers’ Compensation from 1995 to 1997. For the past five years, she has been involved as a member of the Board of Directors of the Work Place Injury Litigation Group. She is also a member of the South Carolina and American Bar Associations and belongs to the American Association for Justice.

After graduating from the University of South Carolina with her law degree in 1982, Ms. Williams went on to serve as a Law Clerk to Associate Justice Julius B. Ness and later for U.S. District Judge G. Ross Anderson, Jr.

He grew up near the Rust Belt city of Youngstown, Ohio, where he was exposed to the blue-collar work ethic and the power of law. His grandfather was a judge, his grandmother was charter member of a nurse’s union and his father worked with the area’s steel industry.

Wilson has been helping asbestos victims since graduating law school in 1988. He joined our firm’s predecessor, Ness, Motley, Loadholt, Richardson & Poole, where he worked with the lawyers who pioneered asbestos and tobacco litigation. The firm put him to work building liability cases against large asbestos companies, preparing cases for trial and assisting with the trials. Within two years, he was co-lead attorney on the case of a Miami tile setter who suffered from asbestosis. The jury returned a $716,000 verdict.

Since that time, Wilson has represented workers and other individuals who developed mesothelioma from asbestos exposure in nearly every state. He has a wealth of industry-specific knowledge about asbestos exposure, the products used at different jobsites and how to maximize financial recovery from the companies that manufactured asbestos products.

The most rewarding and meaningful aspect of his job is that gets to help people who worked hard their entire lives only to find their retirement cut short due to the negligence and willful misconduct of asbestos manufacturers and large employers.

Wilson also enjoys meeting people with fascinating backgrounds. He is proud and honored to represent men and women who worked to win wars and help build the United States.

Wilson is married and has two children in college. He is an avid runner, swimmer and reader of classic literature. He enjoys golf.

attorneys.name: James Christopher Wilson
attorneys.practice_type: General Trial Practice Lawyers in Bamberg, SC
attorneys.bio:
J. Christopher (Chris) Wilson was born and raised in Bamberg, South Carolina. Chris is the first of three brothers born to lifelong Bamberg residents Jimmy and Garnett Wilson. His father Jimmy worked in quality control for over 30 years, and his mother Garnett taught school for over 40 years. They instilled in Chris the values of hard work, honesty, service and integrity – values he ascribes to in his law practice and everyday life.

Chris attended Bamberg public schools and graduated valedictorian from Bamberg-Ehrhardt High School in 1987. He then attended Wofford College where he graduated in 1991 with honors and as a Phi Beta Kappa inductee. While at Wofford College, Chris was active in numerous activities and service organizations and competed on Wofford’s golf team.

Chris was admitted to the South Carolina Bar after receiving his Juris Doctorate degree from the University of South Carolina School of Law in 1994. Chris received several recognitions in Law School, including highest honors in Torts/Injury.

After Law School, he served as a Judicial Clerk for The Honorable Frank McGowan, South Carolina Circuit Court Judge. He then entered the private practice of law, working as an associate for the Bamberg law firm of Early & Ness until 1998 when he formed Wilson Law Firm. Later, he formed Wilson & Luginbill, LLC with Dan Luginbill.

Chris is an experienced attorney whose reputation for representing clients, including his trial work, is well known throughout South Carolina. He has an extensive practice focused primarily on personal injury claims.

Chris is married to Dana Price Wilson (formerly of Marion, SC) and has 3 children – Ansley, Graham and Price. In his spare time, he enjoys coaching youth sports, supporting his children’s sporting events and school activities, volunteering on community boards and supporting local charities. Every once in a while, you can find him golfing – but not near as well as during his Wofford days.

attorneys.name: William Wilson Jr. Esq.
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Goose Creek, SC
attorneys.bio:
William D. Wilson, Jr. is an experienced South Carolina attorney who understands the seriousness of every legal matter and will strive to protect your rights and your future at every juncture. Whether you are facing a divorce and want to protect your financial security or you have been the victim of an automobile accident resulting in personal injury, Mr. Wilson. will aggressively assert your rights and will persevere in obtaining results in your case.

The cornerstone of success is Danny's ability to understand your unique goals and needs, which are pursued with strategy at every stage in your case. This dedication and experience have produced both a reputation for service and a record of results for clients.

As your attorney, William D. Wilson, Jr. will remain accessible, responsive and timely in returning your calls. From your initial consultation through the resolution of your case, you will remain informed and abreast of every development in your case. Throughout the legal process, you may have questions or concerns about the direction of your case. Mr. Wilson will take the time to explore all of your options and alternatives, including any risks that may accompany a decision. You can trust that throughout your case, you will the legal support of an advocate dedicated to the outcome of your case.

Danny Wilson offers individualized legal services tailored to meet the needs of each client. His experience is focused primarily in the areas of insurance defense litigation, personal injury, worker's compensation, family law and criminal DUI defense.

Opening his present practice in Goose Creek in June 2008, Danny has been practicing law since 1995. He began his judicial career as a law clerk for two circuit court judges in South Carolina and a year later, began his trial experience as a state prosecutor. He went on to become a successful insurance defense litigator and continues to use this experience in helping people who have been injured or wrongfully accused.

Mr. Wilson has worked with numerous law firms in South Carolina on personal injury and worker's compensation cases. He is admitted to the bar in South Carolina.

attorneys.bio:
Attorney Thomas W. Winslow is the founding partner of Winslow Law, LLC in Pawleys Island, South Carolina. He has vast experience with medical malpractice and personal injury cases.

He has also worked with employment law, criminal matters, homeowners associations, police and jail misconduct, maritime law, and products liability. Throughout his practice – whether defending the criminally accused, litigating a contentious claim, or researching and preparing legal documentation – he exhibits an ability to represent clients with the highest degree of competence and professionalism.

Tom is licensed to practice in state and federal court in South Carolina (Active) and Washington D.C. (Inactive). This honor allows him access to over 17 state courts through the reciprocity process. He has also been admitted to practice in Georgia, North Carolina, Pennsylvania, Cherokee Reservation, and Tennessee. Along with practicing law, Tom is a certified Notary and Mediator in the State of South Carolina. Mediation is a conflict resolution process in which Attorney Winslow helps aggrieved parties settle their differences and resolve disputes.

attorneys.name: Emma C. Woodham
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Daniel Island, SC
attorneys.bio:
Emma C. Woodham began working at Headley Law Firm as a legal secretary in 2020 and quickly discovered a passion for the practice of law, specifically medical malpractice. That realization prompted Emma to begin her own journey to becoming an attorney and, in December of 2024, she graduated from the Charleston School of Law in Charleston, South Carolina. During the three years during which she attended law school, Emma continued to work full-time at Headley Law Firm as a paralegal. In May of 2025, Emma was admitted to the West Virginia Bar. In her role at Headley Law Firm, Emma enjoys developing relationships with clients and helping them through the process of a lawsuit.

Emma is a native of Lincolnton, Georgia, and obtained her undergraduate degree from Georgia Southern University in 2015, graduating cum laude. After working and living in Savannah, Georgia, for a year after graduation, she moved to South Carolina in 2016 and has called it her home ever since. She and her husband, Ryan, reside in Charleston, South Carolina, with their two dogs, Goose and Poppy. In her spare time, Emma enjoys writing fiction, reading a wide variety of books, traveling and exploring new places, saltwater fishing, college football, and, more recently, Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu.

attorneys.name: P. Brooke Eaves Wright
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury — Plaintiff Lawyers in Myrtle Beach, SC
attorneys.bio:
Brooke Eaves Wright was born and raised in Myrtle Beach, South Carolina and served as Miss Myrtle Beach 2008, 2010, and 2012. Brooke graduated from Clemson University, where she received a B.S. in Marketing and a Minor in Legal Studies in 2011. Thereafter, Brooke received her law degree from the University of South Carolina School of Law in 2014.

During law school, Brooke was a member of the Moot Court Bar and was one of eight students named to the Order of the Barristers in 2012. Brooke competed on the National Competition Team and was one of three Moot Court Bar members selected to represent the USC School of Law in the National Moot Court Competition sponsored by the American College of Trial Lawyers. Brooke was a Top Four Finalist in the Kate Bockman Memorial 2L Moot Court Competition, in which she argued at the South Carolina Court of Appeals. Brooke served as the Associate Justice of Public Relations & Alumni for the Moot Court Bar. Brooke was an Editorial Staff Member of the Journal of Law & Education and received the Best Spader Award for the January 2012 and July 2013 issues of the Journal.

As a Myrtle Beach native, Brooke has always been actively involved in the Myrtle Beach community. Brooke established the Backpack Buddies program in 14 Horry County Schools to provide meals for over 2,100 food insecure children on the weekends. Brooke was recognized with the Presidential Service Award and the Nancy Moore Thurmond Community Service Scholarship for her efforts with the Backpack Buddies program. In addition, Brooke received the Sun News Community Leadership Scholarship for her dedication to community service in the Myrtle Beach community. Brooke is very passionate about community service and she is dedicated to seeking justice for injured individuals and their families.

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury - Plaintiff Lawyers in Columbia, SC
attorneys.bio:
Will Yarborough is a Partner and Attorney at Cavanaugh & Thickens, LLC, an award-winning personal injury and workers’ compensation firm in South Carolina. Cavanaugh & Thickens, LLC was founded in 2017, and since then has recovered millions of dollars in compensation for victims of car accidents, truck accidents, on-the-job injuries, wrongful death, and other accident cases throughout Columbia, Charleston, and the state of South Carolina.

Attorney Will Yarborough’s commitment to his clients and his reputation in the personal injury field has led to numerous awards and accolades, including being recently named a Top 100 Civil Plaintiff Trial Attorney in South Carolina, Top 10 Trucking Trial Lawyer, and Top 25 Motor Vehicle Trial Lawyer by The National Trial Lawyers, Best Lawyers: Ones to Watch for three years running, and more.

Prior to joining Cavanaugh & Thickens, LLC, Will practiced at a defense firm where he represented local and national transportation companies, bars, retailers, medical providers, and insurance companies. He handled hundreds of cases throughout the case lifecycle, and now applies this experience to help injured people get the justice and compensation they deserve.

Will is a native of Columbia, South Carolina, and attended Clemson University for undergrad. Will was a member of the United States Army Reserve, where he served both enlisted time and as an officer upon graduation from Clemson’s Reserve Officer Training Corps. He earned his J.D. from the University of South Carolina and is an active member of the South Carolina Bar, Richland County Bar, and South Carolina Association for Justice.

Animal Bites, Brain Injury, Construction Accidents, Motor Vehicle Accidents, Personal Injury - Plaintiff, Premises Liability - Plaintiff, Trucking Accidents, Wrongful Death

attorneys.name: Adam D. Young
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Charleston, SC
attorneys.bio:
--Former 9th Circuit Solicitor Attorney Serving You--

Adam Young has an AV Preeminent* rating from Martindale-Hubbell. Adam was also selected as a member of The National Trial Lawyers Top 100, which is an invitation-only organization that recognizes the top 100 trial lawyers in each state. During law school, Adam worked for the Navy JAG, NCIS division in Washington, DC and also clerked for the United States Attorney's Office in Charleston. After graduating from law school, Adam began his legal career at the Ninth Circuit Solicitor's Office, focusing his efforts on prosecuting criminal domestic violence cases. Starting his career focusing specifically on prosecuting criminal domestic violence cases provided Adam with a unique opportunity to learn from the ground up the ins and outs of the criminal justice system, including the experience negotiating pleas and trying countless bench trials. Adam was promoted to the violent crime team where he seized the opportunity to handle all types of violent crimes, ranging from assault and battery to drug crimes to armed robberies to attempted murder cases.

Adam has also successfully represented personal injury clients in negotiations, mediations and litigation of their claims. Adam provides a personalized approach towards personal injury cases by not working for big insurance companies or corporate clients. He is working for the individual client and focusing on their needs. Adam's goal is to make sure his clients receive the maximum compensation available, whether that means a trial or through successful pretrial negotiations.

In addition to Adam’s personal injury and criminal defense clients, Adam is the legal advisor for Hunting for Healing Inc., which is a charitable organization aimed at providing positive outdoor events and hunts for disabled United States military veterans and spouses. Adam counsels the organization on legal issues to ensure Hunting for Healing can best serve the military community. Adam also works as a prosecutor for the city of Folly Beach. As a Folly Beach prosecutor, he has gained insight and experience that is ultimately beneficial to his private clients. Courtroom exposure, a sharpened skill set and building a strong reputation as a trial attorney are only a few client benefits. Additionally, this experience has provided him with knowledge regarding what is needed by a prosecutor to convict or prove a case- which, in turn, helps him to understand what is necessary in building the strongest defense possible.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
--Former 9th Circuit Solicitor Attorney Serving You--

Adam Young has an AV Preeminent* rating from Martindale-Hubbell. Adam was also selected as a member of The National Trial Lawyers Top 100, which is an invitation-only organization that recognizes the top 100 trial lawyers in each state. During law school, Adam worked for the Navy JAG, NCIS division in Washington, DC and also clerked for the United States Attorney's Office in Charleston. After graduating from law school, Adam began his legal career at the Ninth Circuit Solicitor's Office, focusing his efforts on prosecuting criminal domestic violence cases. Starting his career focusing specifically on prosecuting criminal domestic violence cases provided Adam with a unique opportunity to learn from the ground up the ins and outs of the criminal justice system, including the experience negotiating pleas and trying countless bench trials. Adam was promoted to the violent crime team where he seized the opportunity to handle all types of violent crimes, ranging from assault and battery to drug crimes to armed robberies to attempted murder cases.

Adam has also successfully represented personal injury clients in negotiations, mediations and litigation of their claims. Adam provides a personalized approach towards personal injury cases by not working for big insurance companies or corporate clients. He is working for the individual client and focusing on their needs. Adam's goal is to make sure his clients receive the maximum compensation available, whether that means a trial or through successful pretrial negotiations.

In addition to Adam’s personal injury and criminal defense clients, Adam is the legal advisor for Hunting for Healing Inc., which is a charitable organization aimed at providing positive outdoor events and hunts for disabled United States military veterans and spouses. Adam counsels the organization on legal issues to ensure Hunting for Healing can best serve the military community. Adam also works as a prosecutor for the city of Folly Beach. As a Folly Beach prosecutor, he has gained insight and experience that is ultimately beneficial to his private clients. Courtroom exposure, a sharpened skill set and building a strong reputation as a trial attorney are only a few client benefits. Additionally, this experience has provided him with knowledge regarding what is needed by a prosecutor to convict or prove a case- which, in turn, helps him to understand what is necessary in building the strongest defense possible.

attorneys.bio:
J. Rutledge Young, Jr. focuses his practice on health care, professional liability, and complex business issues. He is chair of Young Clement Rivers, LLP's Health Care and Special Task Litigation Practice Groups and is a former managing partner of the firm. He holds the highest professional AV Preeminent rating in the Martindale-Hubbell Law Directory and has been listed for more than 25 years in the Best Lawyers in America and for more than 10 in years in Chambers USA America's Leading Business Lawyers. He was also selected as a Best Lawyer in America for Bet-the-Company Litigation for 2007, 2008, and 2009. A former president of Historic Charleston Foundation, he has been active in preservation and conservation organizations.

J. Rutledge Young, Jr. has served on the Charleston City Council and the South Carolina Supreme Court's Board of Commissioners on Grievances and Discipline. He is a Diplomate of the American Board of Trial Advocates and a Fellow in the American College of Trial Lawyers. He is active in the South Carolina Bar and served as president in 1994-1995.

He is a veteran of the U.S. Army and was awarded a bronze star during service as Captain of MACV Advisory Team No.7 from 1968 to 1970 in Long Kanh Province, Republic of Vietnam.

Ken is a Vietnam veteran and former prosecutor. During his time as a prosecutor, he helped prosecute the most infamous serial killer in South Carolina history Donald "Pee Wee" Gaskins. After serving as an Assistant Solicitor, he opened his own private practice in the 1980's.

Personal Life:

Ken was born and raised in the City of Sumter, where he graduated from Edmunds High School. He is a lifelong member and Former Elder of the First Presbyterian Church in Sumter, SC.

Ken is a loving Father, Husband and Grandfather. Ken and his wife have two children and 4 grandchildren.

When he is not making fierce arguments in the courtroom, he enjoys spending time with his family and playing with his grandchildren.

attorneys.name: Kelley F. Young
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Charleston, SC
attorneys.bio:
--A former Judge and former prosecutor working for you--

Kelley Young grew up in the Lowcountry an after graduating magna cum laude from law school, she immediately moved back to the area because of her passion to help those in her community. During law school, Kelley clerked for the United States Attorney's Office as well as for two judges in the criminal arena. She also successfully argued cases as a Certified Legal Intern for the Department of Homeland Security, Immigration and Customs Enforcement Division. Kelley practiced as an Assistant Solicitor in Charleston for several years, where she was selected to focus primarily on litigating violent crimes and larger narcotics cases towards the end of her prosecution career.

Kelley left the prosecutor's office when she was appointed by the Governor of South Carolina to become a Magistrate Judge for Charleston County. As a Magistrate Judge, Kelley gained invaluable experience by holding bond hearings, preliminary hearings, traffic court as well as eviction hearings for all of Charleston County. Because of her passion to fight for others in the Lowcountry where she grew up, Kelley resigned as a Magistrate Judge to join Adam Young in private practice.

Kelley’s diverse trial experience as a prosecutor and her time as a Magistrate Judge has led her to fully understand the inner workings of all stages in the criminal justice system-including how to assess the weaknesses of each criminal case during preliminary hearings or pre-indictment stages, negotiate bonds and plea agreements between attorneys and judges, and zealously protect and defend the rights of her clients. When she is not working for her personal injury or criminal defense clients, Kelley prosecutes cases for the City of Folly Beach. Kelley's litigation background and unique experience as a local Judge make her a strong advocate for all of her clients.
